peer_results.rationale: The provided candidates for AMD discuss working capital components and net cash used in investing activities (acquisitions, short-term investments, property purchases), which do not address the specific definition, purpose, or non-GAAP nature of Adjusted Free Cash Flow as described in Intel's disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of November 3, 2024, the company's primary liquidity sources included $9,348 million in cash and cash equivalents, expected operating cash flows, and $7.5 billion in available capacity under its unsecured revolving credit facility.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Broadcom both explicitly identify operating cash flows as a primary component of their liquidity resources. Intel states that adjusted free cash flow is used to assess sources of liquidity and capital resources, rooted in operating cash flow. Broadcom lists cash expected to be generated from operations as one of its three primary sources of liquidity, demonstrating a similar reliance on operational cash generation for liquidity management.

sentences.text: This measure is used by management when assessing our sources of liquidity, capital resources, and quality of earnings and provides an additional means to evaluate the cash flow trends of our business.

Our primary sources of liquidity as of November 3, 2024 consisted of: (i) $9,348 million in cash and cash equivalents, (ii) cash we expect to generate from operations and (iii) available capacity under our $7.5 billion unsecured revolving credit facility.

comparisons.peer_summary: For 2024, net cash used for investing activities consisted primarily of $8.39 billion in expenditures for property, plant, and equipment and $205 million in net outflows from available-for-sale securities, partially offset by $315 million in government incentives for capital expenditures.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose capital expenditure adjustments to cash flow metrics, specifically accounting for government incentives. Intel defines adjusted free cash flow by subtracting capital expenditures net of government incentives and partner contributions. Micron reports net cash used in investing activities which includes significant expenditures for property, plant, and equipment partially offset by government incentives, highlighting a shared industry practice of utilizing public funding to offset capital intensity in this peer group.

sentences.text: Adjusted free cash flow is operating cash flow adjusted for (1) additions to property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from capital-related government incentives and net partner contributions, (2) payments on finance leases, and (3) proceeds from the McAfee equity sale in 2022.

Investing Activities: For 2024, net cash used for investing activities consisted primarily of $8.39 billion of expenditures for property, plant, and equipment; and $205 million of net outflows from purchases, maturities, and sales of available-for-sale securities; partially offset by contributions of $315 million received from government incentives to offset capital expenditures.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of fiscal year 2024, the company held $26.0 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, asserting sufficient liquidity to meet operating requirements, including a $1.3 billion debt repayment in fiscal 2025 and share purchases, for at least the next twelve months.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both emphasize the sufficiency of liquidity generated from operations to meet future requirements. Intel uses adjusted free cash flow (derived from operating cash flow) to evaluate cash flow trends and liquidity. NVIDIA explicitly states that cash generated by operations is a primary source of liquidity and that existing cash and operating cash flows are sufficient to meet operating requirements and capital obligations.

sentences.text: This measure is used by management when assessing our sources of liquidity, capital resources, and quality of earnings and provides an additional means to evaluate the cash flow trends of our business.
Our primary sources of liquidity are our cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, and the cash generated by our operations.

We believe that we have sufficient liquidity to meet our operating requirements for at least the next twelve months, and for the foreseeable future, including our future supply obligations and $1.3 billion of debt repayment due in fiscal year 2025 and share purchases.
